paper_metadata.title: Competition of Mechanical Properties Between Mg-Al and Mg-Sn Alloys at Different Temperatures and Corresponding Microstructure Characterization
paper_metadata.journal: Journal of Materials Engineering and Performance

evidence.quote: The differences in mechanical properties at different temperatures and microstructure between extruded-aged Mg-11Al-1Ag (abbreviated as A11-Q alloy) and extruded-aged Mg-8Sn-2Al-1.5Bi-1Ag alloys (abbreviated as TA82-BQ alloy) were systematically investigated.

The differences in mechanical properties at different temperatures and microstructure between extruded-aged Mg-11Al-1Ag (abbreviated as A11-Q alloy) and extruded-aged Mg-8Sn-2Al-1.5Bi-1Ag alloys (abbreviated as TA82-BQ alloy) were systematically investigated.
extruded-aged Mg-11Al-1Ag (abbreviated as A11-Q alloy)
extruded-aged Mg-8Sn-2Al-1.5Bi-1Ag alloys (abbreviated as TA82-BQ alloy)
The melt was held at 710 °C for 30 min and 750 °C for 20 min, and then it was poured into a steel mold when the melt temperature slowed down to 700 °C.
The homogenized temperature and time of as-cast A11-Q alloys were 350 °C and 2 h, reepectively.
And the homogenized A11-Q alloys were solid solutioned at 430 °C for 20 h followed by water quenching.
Both solid solutioned alloys were extruded with an extrusion ration of 25 at 320 °C by hydraulic machine.
The further aging temperatures and times of extruded A11-Q and TA82-BQ alloys were 200 °C for 10 h and 200 °C for 130 h, respectively.
The melt was held at 710 °C for 30 min and 750 °C for 20 min, and then it was poured into a steel mold when the melt temperature slowed down to 700 °C.
The homogenized temperature and time of as-cast TA82-BQ alloy were 400 °C and 16 h, respectively.
And the homogenized TA82-BQ alloys were solid solutioned at 480 °C for 4 h followed by water quenching.
Both solid solutioned alloys were extruded with an extrusion ration of 25 at 320 °C by hydraulic machine.
The further aging temperatures and times of extruded A11-Q and TA82-BQ alloys were 200 °C for 10 h and 200 °C for 130 h, respectively.

Furthermore, a relatively stronger basal texture with the maximum intensity of 6.22 formed in extruded-aged TA82-BQ alloy.

Figure 7 shows the representative precipitates morphology in extruded-aged A11-Q and TA82-BQ alloys by TEM results, which suggests that numerous fine precipitates are observed in extruded-aged A11-Q and TA82-BQ alloys.
Figure 7(b) shows that fewer rodlike precipitates and more ellipsoidal precipitates are observed in extruded-aged TA82-BQ alloy.
Furthermore, a number of rodlike and ellipsoidal precipitates form in both extruded-aged A11-Q and TA82-BQ alloys, which plays a role on precipitation strengthening.

Furthermore, some Al and Sn atoms still exist in a-Mg matrix and play the role of solid solution strengthening as shown in Figs. 8, 9.
The strength increment is attributed to grain boundaries in part, which can be explained by Hall-Petch relationship (Ref 41, 42).
